Definition: Jahats or Jahtsah, a place East of the Jordan
BiblicalUsage: Jahaz was a town east of the Jordan, in the land of Reuben, where Israel met Sihon king of the Amorites in battle. Moses recalls that Sihon came out against Israel to fight at Jahaz, and Israel struck him down and took his land. The town later passed to the Levites, listed among their cities with its pasturelands.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God gave Israel the victory at Jahaz before they ever set foot in the promised land, and the town kept the memory. What He wins for His people, He also gives them to keep.
